text:
lia: onboarding Cassiopeia-8B (int4) today. quick smoke passed but we see systematic token-alignment drift vs fp16 reference after ~150 tokens. suspect rotary packing/tiling mismatch. attaching tiny repro below.

anna: can you show the tokenizer outputs around the drift point? BOS/EOS and any sentinel ids?

sam: saw similar pattern with another int4 build — embeddings stay stable first 128 tokens then offset appears. often a headwise/pack difference. :thinking_face:

lia: repro snippet:
```python
# minimal repro to show token id stream vs cached kv lookup
text = 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.'
toks = tok.encode(text)  # huggingface-style wrapper
print(toks[:10])
# -> [1, 345, 2345, 78, 9001, 14, 56, 9, 3]
# run model once fp16 then int4 and compare logits at step 160
```

kevin: are you using per-head rotary application or per-layer interleaved tiling? Cassiopeia's weights were exported with a "lattice" pack (packed heads contiguous) which our import historically mapped to alternating head layout.

lia: export metadata shows: `rotary_pack: lattice` and `rotary_dim: 64` in model.json. our runtime expects `rotary_dim` to be divided by heads->32 per head. mismatch may shift phase indices.

anna: if the exporter used head-major packing but we interpret as head-minor, KV cache token indices will misalign. easy test: swap head stride during load and run the same prompt; if logits re-align then it's packing.

sam: quick check command: `rwi-convert --input cassiopeia.bin --rotary-layout=guess --dump-rotary-map` will print mapping. Lia, can you run that on your bundle?

lia: ran it, output snippet: `rotary_map: [0,2,4,6,1,3,5,7,...]` which looks interleaved odd-even. our loader currently assumes sequential `[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7]`.

kevin: bingo. that interleaving would produce the ~128 token delayed drift since prefix caching expects same head ordering across calls.

ci-bot: CI bench: cassiopeia-int4-smoke — failure at 00:14:03 with perplexity delta +0.17 vs fp16 baseline. full logs: https://ci.internal/runs/2319

anna: two mitigation paths: 1) at load-time remap rotary keys to our canonical head order (cheap), 2) add runtime toggle to interpret lattice packing (longer). I'd prefer remap for now.

lia: re-mapping looks straightforward. small patch idea: after loading qkv weights run reshape 
```python
# pseudo
arr = arr.reshape(n_heads, head_dim, ...)
arr = arr[reorder_idx]
arr = arr.reshape(original_shape)
```
keep checksum to validate.

sam: also add a unit test: run 200-token insist prompt both fp16 and int4 after remap and assert top-1 tokens equal for first 180 tokens. catches future regressions.

kevin: watch out for tokenizer boundary: some vocab exports put sentinel tokens into top-256 slot which changes those numeric ids — make sure we compare semantic tokens not just raw ids occasionally.

lia: noted. I will: run remap, add checksum, add unit test, and re-run smoke CI. ETA end of day.

anna: if you need a quick stopgap, we can add a per-model metadata flag `rotary_layout: interleaved` in model.json and the loader will auto-apply remap. but long-term canonicalization on export side is ideal.

sam: :thumbsup: agree. Also add a small eval comparing generation ngram overlap on helpfulness set — to ensure quality not just logits match.

lia: logging next steps in the PR description. ping me if CI still shows drift. thanks all. :raised_hands:
